name: Erik Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the Work Futures Panel, an independent group with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. Could you walk me through a normal workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and build new power lines for an electricity company, usually out on feeder jobs that carry power to farms and new buildings. My vocational certificate and apprenticeship taught me to measure twice before we set a pole, and these days I bring younger workers along. I like watching a long straight span go up; the travel and missed evenings at home wear me down.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is your household balancing, and do you use AI at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My spouse handles accounts for a small plumbing firm, and our two children are school age. My lineworker pay is above the usual rate, we have a mortgage and about ten months of expenses saved, and several utilities nearby have similar crews. I use AI now and then to understand a new fitting, but I still check the actual drawings and the site survey.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the construction crew our feeder lines still need poles set straight and wire tensioned correctly. The AI can trim an office form, but no one is taking a mud-splashed digger away because of a paragraph generator.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The work looks steady and I earn well enough to have saved ten months of expenses. My spouse runs the accounts for a small plumbing firm, and the mortgage is manageable if we keep both jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep building the new feeder out toward the farms and use my usual notebook for material counts. When the office sends an AI-drafted list, I'll check pole lengths and fittings against our site survey before it goes to stores.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, and I would enjoy less form-filling. I still think the children should learn to make something with their hands as well as read a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell a new apprentice about the material list?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show a new apprentice how a wrong pole length changes the whole span, then have him measure the distance himself. A neat list is no good if the wire hangs too low. A neat computer list is no good if the power wire hangs too low.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does the reserve change your plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our older child needs school supplies this term, but that is in the regular budget. The ten-month reserve stays for a real interruption, not a new gadget.

say: **Feeder construction** still needs crews to set poles and tension wires correctly.
**AI paperwork** may be quicker, but material counts must fit the surveyed site.
think: Our **ten-month reserve** and manageable mortgage make this a steady picture for home.
I welcome fewer **forms** without expecting a major change to line building.
do: **Keep** building the farm feeder with the existing crew.
**Check** office material lists against pole measurements and site survey before ordering.
feel: **Calm** about income and glad to lose a little paperwork.
S0.quote: A neat computer list is no good if the power wire hangs too low.
fieldNote: He anchors the scenario in **physical measurements**, not broad claims about technology.
His **strong reserve** and current construction work leave little immediate pressure on household income.

steps.text: Keep building farm feeder with existing construction crew

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI could plan the order of jobs and buy fittings, while robots take longer to set poles in rough ground. I would ask the company to show the crew where the new plans came from before we drive an hour to the site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My building work looks safer than the office's buying role, but a faster schedule might cost us overtime. That extra pay has helped with the mortgage even though we have a good reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare two AI-generated build schedules with our actual site access and delivery times. If the system survives that test, I'll ask to learn it on paid time, then keep a separate note of overtime hours for the first year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about hours, though I do not expect to be out of work. I can use a proven tool without letting it set the pace of a crew in bad weather.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the AI schedule misses a wire delivery?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would call dispatch and delay the crew before the lorry leaves the depot. A missing spool is cheaper to fix there than beside a field gate. A missing wire spool is cheaper to fix at the depot than beside a field gate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you show overtime has changed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show the supervisor the missed deliveries and overtime log, not just say the software feels wrong. If hours fall enough to change the household budget, we'll review expenses then.

say: **AI schedules** must match deliveries and site access before a construction crew travels.
**Robots** should change rough-ground pole work more slowly than office buying and planning.
think: Our **overtime** might shrink if the company packs jobs more tightly.
My **line-building wage** should remain, but a lower total pay packet would touch the mortgage budget.
do: **Compare** two generated build schedules against delivery dates and site access.
**Learn** the planner on paid time if the trial works, while logging overtime hours.
feel: **Anxious** about overtime and rushing, while expecting to keep the core job.
S1.quote: A missing wire spool is cheaper to fix at the depot than beside a field gate.
fieldNote: He identifies **overtime loss** as the household risk in moderate disruption.
He accepts a **paid tool trial** if it stands up to real site and delivery checks.

steps.text: Compare two AI build schedules against deliveries and site access
Learn company planner on paid time if trial proves reliable

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew thinking AI by 2028 might write every build plan before a person sees it. Field robots around 2031 worry me more, because a machine that sets poles could take away the hours that pay our households. A pole-setting robot could take the hours that pay our family mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could use the ten-month reserve and there are other utilities nearby, but their construction crews might also shrink. My spouse's accounts job could change in 2028, before anyone puts a robot on our feeder line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask my supervisor for the construction staffing plan and my spouse will ask the plumbing firm what happens to its accounts work. We'll stop the planned camper purchase and send the monthly amount we meant for it into savings from our pay; if shifts are cut, I'll apply for an open line post nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, not lost. Ten months is enough to make calls and choose, but it is not enough to carry two children through years without proper wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which family expense changes first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would first cancel the camper purchase and keep school fees and mortgage payments in the regular budget. I would explain to the children that we are making room, not telling them I have been fired.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a robot course worthwhile?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take a paid company course on testing pole-setting robots if it came with a real vacancy or roster. I would not pay for a generic course with no employer willing to use the skill.

say: **2028 thinking AI** reaches planning and accounts before field robots arrive around 2031.
The electricity company should publish **construction staffing** before promising every crew a place.
think: Our **ten-month reserve** gives us time, though both household jobs could face cuts.
Nearby utilities may have **open posts**, but they might be changing their crews too.
do: **Ask** both employers for staffing plans before the 2028 thinking shift.
**Cancel** the planned camper purchase and cut that discretionary spending.
**Save** the camper payment amount from wages while both jobs hold.
feel: **Anxious** about two incomes and the later loss of construction hours.
S2.quote: A pole-setting robot could take the hours that pay our family mortgage.
fieldNote: He sees the **accounts job** at risk sooner than his own field construction work.
His saving is **new money from wages**, redirected from a planned camper payment.
A robot course requires a **paid place** tied to real work; he has no such offer.

steps.text: Cancel planned camper purchase and cut discretionary spending
Save monthly camper amount from wages while both jobs hold
Ask both employers for staffing plans before 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the five-year runway is long enough to run a pole-setting robot beside a normal crew and count what it actually does. Thinking AI by 2031 changes schedules first, and the field robot question comes around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn to supervise that equipment if the company proves it safe. What I fear is losing construction hours gradually while being told a new supervisor job may appear someday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll put my name down for a company-paid field trial if one opens, and log how often the machine needs a human to reset or inspect it. We'll add a regular extra mortgage payment from my base wage, stopping it if my spouse's accounts hours fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but less hurried than in the fast picture. I want five years of evidence, not a shiny one-day display.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the field trial credible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would make them run the robot on our sloped access road and measure the finished pole alignment. If it fails, I would write down the fault before anyone calls the trial a success. A shiny pole-setting robot display cannot show me whether the machine works on our sloped road.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What funds the extra mortgage payment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra payment comes from delaying a kitchen refit, and only while both wages remain. If accounts hours drop, the kitchen can wait and the mortgage goes back to its normal payment.

say: **Field trials** should use sloped roads and measurable pole alignment before crews change.
**2031 schedules** will change earlier than 2034 field robotics on construction sites.
think: A paid **robot oversight role** might suit me, but no vacancy is promised.
Gradually fewer **building hours** could hurt before a formal job cut arrives.
do: **Join** a company-paid pole robot trial if offered and log failures.
**Overpay** the mortgage from postponed kitchen spending while both wages hold.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, with time to gather evidence and reduce debt.
S3.quote: A shiny pole-setting robot display cannot show me whether the machine works on our sloped road.
fieldNote: He sets a **measurable field test** rather than accepting a demonstration.
His mortgage overpayment depends on **both incomes** and a delayed kitchen refit.
He distinguishes possible **oversight work** from an actual paid vacancy.

steps.text: Join company-paid pole robot trial if offered and log failures
Overpay mortgage from postponed kitchen budget while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade gives apprentices time to learn both safe line building and new machines. Thinking AI in 2036 changes the drawings; capable field robots around 2039 might change how a feeder is built.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 56 near the robot date and could still work as a site inspector if there are real posts. With ten months saved and the mortgage lower by then, I would not need to guess about an early retirement date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep my certificate and safety tickets current, ask yearly about paid field inspection openings, and bring an apprentice along on actual survey days. If a clear company training route appears, I'll take it on paid time while keeping the construction wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm enough to plan, though I would miss teaching a full crew to string its first long span. Ten years gives my children room to finish school without a sudden income shock.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children about trades?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell them a trade is worth considering when they can see the work and the training is real. I would not push either child into electricity just because their father has done well in it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you need before moving to inspection?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd need the inspection role's wage, hours and travel area in writing. A title that pays less than the mortgage needs would not be a workable plan for us. A field inspection title that pays less than our mortgage needs is not a plan for my family.

say: **Apprentices** should learn physical line safety alongside new equipment over the decade.
**2039 field robots** may change feeder construction after drawings change in 2036.
think: A paid **inspection vacancy** could suit me at 56 if its hours and wage work for home.
Our **reserve** and a smaller mortgage give us choices without assuming early retirement.
do: **Renew** line certificates and safety tickets while continuing feeder construction.
**Ask** annually about paid inspection openings and their wages and travel area.
feel: **Calm** about the longer runway, with some sadness about changing construction crews.
S4.quote: A field inspection title that pays less than our mortgage needs is not a plan for my family.
fieldNote: He would move to inspection only for a **real paid post** with suitable travel and wages.
The longer horizon lets him preserve **apprentice teaching** and family income through school years.

steps.text: Renew line certificate and safety tickets while building feeders
Check paid inspection openings annually for wages and travel area

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my spouse's accounts work could change quickly, then robots reach our construction work around 2031. The electricity company showing real crew numbers and offering paid field trials tied to jobs would help us decide what to do.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Who measures the hours that disappear before anyone loses a job? A construction crew can keep the same names on paper while the overtime that paid a mortgage quietly goes away. I would keep that number in my notebook. A power-line construction crew can keep the same names on paper while its mortgage-paying overtime quietly goes away.

headlineQuote: A power-line construction crew can keep the same names on paper while its mortgage-paying overtime quietly goes away.
portrait: **Erik**, 43, builds new electricity feeders and teaches apprentices after a vocational certificate and apprenticeship.
His **higher pay**, ten-month reserve and nearby utilities help, though the mortgage still relies partly on overtime.
He uses AI **occasionally** and wants generated plans checked against material deliveries and site measurements.
He would test **pole robots** in real conditions and consider inspection only with a paid post that meets household needs.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink his spouse's accounts work before robots reach construction around 2031.
whatWouldHelp: Published **crew numbers** and paid field trials tied to actual jobs would make household planning possible.
